title: Finiteness of scalar classes of units with bounded inverse coordinates
statement:
Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $A$ be a commutative unital $F$-algebra which is an integral domain, meaning $1\ne0$ and that a product of two nonzero elements is nonzero. Let $V,W\subseteq A$ be $F$-vector subspaces, each finite-dimensional [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace]. A unit of $A$ is an element $a$ possessing a multiplicative inverse $a^{-1}$ in $A$. Then the set
$$\{a\in A^\times:a\in V,\ a^{-1}\in W\}/\mathord{\sim}$$
is finite, where $a\sim a'$ means that $a'=c a$ for some $c\in F^\times$, viewed in $A$ through its structure homomorphism. No finite generation hypothesis on $A$ is imposed.

source.place: Agent-formulated auxiliary lemma for Milne, Algebraic Groups, Proposition 12.48 (literature/milne-algebraic-groups_iAG2017.pdf, pp.246--247). Projective incidence proof uses Tag 01WD (constructions-lemma-segre-embedding), morphisms.tex Tag 0EKE (lemma-proper-ample-delete-affine), and Tag 01WN (lemma-finite-proper). The source tags supply the geometric tools, not this exact algebraic statement; the full agent argument is retained in report.md.

proof.text: If $V=0$ or $W=0$, the asserted set is empty, since a unit in a nonzero ring is nonzero. Otherwise choose bases $v_1,\ldots,v_r$ of $V$ and $w_1,\ldots,w_s$ of $W$, where $r,s\geq1$. The structure map $F\to A$ is injective: its kernel is an ideal of the field and cannot contain $1$. Thus $1\ne0$ spans a copy of $F$ in $A$. The subspace $U=F1+\sum_{i,j}Fv_iw_j$ has finite dimension; extend $e_0=1$ to a basis $e_0,e_1,\ldots,e_t$ of $U$. Write $v_iw_j=\sum_{k=0}^t c_{kij}e_k$. These are finitely many coefficients in $F$, regardless of the dimension or finite generation of $A$.

source.place: Agent finite-coordinate preparation for the projective incidence argument supporting Milne Proposition 12.48; no finite-type assumption on A.

proof.text:
Put $R=F[z_{ij}]$ ($1\le i\le r$, $1\le j\le s$), graded with each $z_{ij}$ of degree one, so $\mathbf P^{rs-1}_F=\operatorname{Proj}R$. Let $\ell_k=\sum_{i,j}c_{kij}z_{ij}$ for $0\le k\le t$, and let $J\subseteq R$ be the ideal generated by the quadrics $z_{ij}z_{i'j'}-z_{ij'}z_{i'j}$ and by $\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_t$. Its generators are homogeneous, so $R/J$ is graded and $R	o R/J$ is a surjective degree-preserving morphism of graded $F$-algebras. Regard both as graded quasi-coherent algebras on $\operatorname{Spec}F$, whose relative Proj is the plain Proj by clause (1) of [prop-nagata-relative-proj-functoriality]; clause (3) then makes $Z=\operatorname{Proj}(R/J)	o\mathbf P^{rs-1}_F$ a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Rational points: the $D_+(z_{ab})$ cover $\operatorname{Proj}R$ and $D_+(z_{ab})=\operatorname{Spec}R_{(z_{ab}),0}$ by [prop-nagata-proj-standard-open]. An $F$-point of $Z$ in $D_+(z_{ab})$ is therefore an $F$-algebra map sending $z_{ij}/z_{ab}\mapsto\zeta_{ij}$ with $\zeta_{ab}=1$ and $g(\zeta)=0$ for every homogeneous $g\in J$. Conversely, every $\zeta
e0$ killed by $J$ gives one, on a chart with $\zeta_{ab}
e0$, and $\zeta,\lambda\zeta$ give the same point. The quadrics give $\zeta_{ij}=x_iy_j$ with $x_i=\zeta_{ib}$, $y_j=\zeta_{aj}$, so $x_a=y_b=1$. Put $v=\sum_ix_iv_i
e0$ and $w=\sum_jy_jw_j
e0$. Then $vw=\sum_k\ell_k(\zeta)e_k$, and $\ell_1(\zeta)=\cdots=\ell_t(\zeta)=0$ says $vw=\ell_0(\zeta)1$. The cases $t=0$ and $\ell_0=0$ are allowed.

source.place: Tag 01N0 (lemma-surjective-graded-rings-map-proj): surjective graded map gives a closed immersion of Proj; Tag 01M4 (lemma-standard-open) for the charts; agent rank-one quadrics replace the Segre image of Tag 01WD.

proof.text: The projection $\mathbf P^{rs-1}_F\to\operatorname{Spec}F$ is proper by [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper]. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper](c) to the closed immersion just constructed proves that $Z\to\operatorname{Spec}F$ is proper. In particular $Z$ is of finite type over $F$, by the definition of properness. This is a property of the finite-coordinate parameter scheme $Z$, not of $\operatorname{Spec}A$.

source.place: Tag 01WC (lemma-locally-projective-proper), proof for projective space; Tag 01W5 (lemma-closed-immersion-proper), with Tag 01W3 (lemma-composition-proper).

proof.text: Let $C=Z\setminus D_+(\ell_0)$, the closed subset of points of $Z$ at which $\ell_0$ vanishes. By step 3, $Z$ is of finite type over $F$. Suppose $C$ were nonempty. Applying [lem-sc-lft-over-field-jacobson-space] to $Z$ and the closed subset $C$ gives a closed point $b$ of $Z$ lying in $C$: an empty set is not dense in a nonempty space. By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-point-residue-field-base], its residue field is $F$ via the structure map. Thus $b$ is an $F$-point. By step 2 it has coordinates $\zeta_{ij}=x_iy_j$ and gives nonzero $v\in V$, $w\in W$ with $vw=\ell_0(\zeta)1$. Since $b\notin D_+(\ell_0)$, the chart function $\ell_0/z_{ab}$ vanishes at $b$, so $\ell_0(\zeta)=0$ and $vw=0$ in $A$. This contradicts the domain hypothesis. Therefore $C$ is empty, and the open subscheme $Z\cap D_+(\ell_0)$ is all of $Z$. No assertion about $A\otimes_F K$ for extension fields $K$ is needed.

source.place: varieties.tex Tag 0478 (lemma-locally-finite-type-Jacobson); morphisms.tex Tag 01TB (lemma-jacobson-finite-type-points) and algebra.tex Tag 00FV (theorem-nullstellensatz); agent domain contradiction.

proof.text: By [prop-nagata-proj-standard-open], the standard open $D_+(\ell_0)$ in $\mathbf P^{rs-1}_F=\operatorname{Proj}F[z_{ij}]$ is affine, with coordinate ring $(F[z_{ij}]_{\ell_0})_0$. The affine description of a closed immersion in [def-weil-closed-immersion] identifies its intersection with the closed subscheme $Z$ with the spectrum of a quotient of this coordinate ring. Hence $Z\cap D_+(\ell_0)$ is affine. This open equals $Z$ by the preceding step, so $Z$ is affine. If $\ell_0=0$ the standard open is empty and the same argument says $Z$ is empty; no nonzero-section hypothesis was inserted.

source.place: Tags 01M4 (lemma-standard-open), 01M7 (lemma-proj-sheaves), and 01MB (lemma-proj-scheme): standard opens of Proj are affine; explicit hyperplane complement replaces morphisms.tex Tag 0EKE (lemma-proper-ample-delete-affine).

proof.text: The structure map of $Z$ is affine, since $Z$ and $\operatorname{Spec}F$ are affine, and it is proper by step 3. By [lem-sfb-affine-proper-finite] it is finite. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-closed-map-finite-fibres](2), its fibre over the unique point of $\operatorname{Spec}F$, namely the whole underlying point set of $Z$, is finite.

source.place: Tag 01WN (lemma-finite-proper); Tag 02NU (lemma-finite-quasi-finite) and Tag 02NH (lemma-quasi-finite) for finite fibres.

proof.text: The map $Z(F)\to |Z|$ sending a rational point to its support is injective. Indeed two rational points with the same support belong to a common affine open $\operatorname{Spec}C$ and give $F$-algebra maps $C\to F$ with the same maximal kernel $\mathfrak m$. Each induced injection $C/\mathfrak m\to F$ fixes the subfield $F$, so it is surjective and inverse to the structure map $F\to C/\mathfrak m$. Consequently the two maps are equal. Thus $Z(F)$ is finite by step 6. This argument permits nilpotents in $Z$.

source.place: Agent elementary affine-coordinate check that an F-rational point is determined by its support.

proof.text:
Send a unit $a\in V$ with $a^{-1}\in W$ to the point $\zeta_{ij}=x_iy_j$, where $a=\sum_ix_iv_i$ and $a^{-1}=\sum_jy_jw_j$. Then $\zeta
e0$, the quadrics vanish at $\zeta$, and $\sum_k\ell_k(\zeta)e_k=aa^{-1}=e_0$. Hence $\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_t$ vanish and $\zeta$ is an $F$-point of $Z$ by step 2. Replacing $a$ by $ca$ for $c\in F^	imes$ replaces $x$ by $cx$ and $y$ by $c^{-1}y$, leaving $\zeta$ unchanged. Conversely, if $a,a'$ give the same point, then $x'_iy'_j=\lambda x_iy_j$ for some $\lambda\in F^	imes$. Choosing $j$ with $y_j
e0$ shows that $x'$ is a scalar multiple of $x$, that is $a'=ca$. Hence this map induces an injection of the quotient in the statement into $Z(F)$, which is finite by step 7. In fact it is onto: an $F$-point gives $v,w$ with $vw=d1$, $d=\ell_0(\zeta)$, and $d
e0$ by step 4, since the point lies in $D_+(\ell_0)$. Therefore $v$ is a unit with inverse $d^{-1}w\in W$, and it maps to the given point. The quotient is finite, as required.

source.place: Agent final projective-coordinate identification of bounded-inverse scalar classes; uses the incidence equations and empty-boundary result proved above.

Auxiliary to Milne Proposition 12.48, not a claim that Milne states this lemma.
